newsitem.title: USA: Pan Am sees no layoffs from Carnival deal.
newsitem.headline: Pan Am sees no layoffs from Carnival deal.

text.p: Pan American World Airways Chief Executive Martin Shugrue on Friday said he expected no layoffs in the wake of the carrier's acquisition of Carnival Air Lines.
The combined company would have about 2,075 employees.
"We don't anticipate any layoffs at all," Shugrue said at a news conference.
He also said he expected the combined companies would add positions over time, although he did not elaborate.
As part of the proposed combination of the two airlines, Micky Arison, Carnival Air's primary shareholder, will make a $30 million capital investment in Pan Am.
Pan Am has also arranged for a private placement of up to $30 million in a new series of preferred stock.

Shugrue said he expected the money would be spent for working capital purposes and for internal investment, such as possible purchases of additional aircraft and conversion of Carnival's fleet to conform with Pan Am's.
"The capital infusion adds to the company's liquidity for working capital purposes and internal investment. It costs money to paint airplanes. It costs money to buy seats," he said.
